items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: I've been looking forward to playing with Jay McShann... I've never worked with him before... I know all about Jay McShann, but I've never had the pleasure.

ctx.x: You turned away people at that auditorium. It was marvelous.

Yes, and I would certainly like to do some more of that. I enjoyed doing that. On June 15th, I am playing with Jay McShann at the University of California at San Diego. I've done a couple of concerts down there with Bert Turetzky, who is a bass professor. We did some duos of Duke Ellington music, too, things that he put together called "Down In Duke's Basement."

Incidentally, coming back to the European trip with the James Newton Quintet, most of the music was original music except for two things that I arranged for the group. One was "Lush Life" featuring tuba and bassoon, and the other was "Chelsea Bridge" which was a tuba solo. And I'll come back to another point.
